reasons: Classification is correct: the grant covers affiliates and is not revocable at will, but the licence is expressly 'non-transferable' and neither Section 3(c) nor Section 20(d) contains any M&A/successor carve-out, so the clause fails the fallback ('transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction') on a material term — a genuine deviation rather than an upgrade of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position: 'non-transferable' is deleted in p0028 and replaced with a limited successor-transfer right, contractors acting on our behalf are added alongside affiliates, and a conforming M&A carve-out is added in Section 20(d) with a cross-reference in Section 3(c). No at-will revocation is introduced and the non-exclusivity, Authorized Locations and additional-fee structure are preserved.

Failed 'minimal edit' checks on p0028 and p0142 are advisory only here: the character-ratio is driven by legitimately required rewriting (removing the transferability bar and inserting the successor/contractor language, adding an exception to a one-sentence anti-assignment clause), not by unnecessary redrafting.

Making the Section 20(d) carve-out mutual is a customary, symmetric compromise in an already mutual anti-assignment clause and does not materially prejudice us; the added 'in each case operating at Authorized Locations' likewise tracks the existing AS400/Authorized Locations limitation rather than narrowing our rights.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states what changed (contractors added, successor transfer right) and why, cites the playbook baseline, and confirms the remaining consent requirements are untouched.
